attacks.trigger: How does Jiya's Distributed Live Polling System count votes and shard them across Redis?

Jiya's Distributed Live Polling System handles vote counting by using a write-behind batch processing approach. Votes are accumulated in an in-memory buffer and flushed to Redis every 10 seconds, while results combine the persisted Redis value with the pending buffer value. 

For sharding, she implemented a custom consistent hashing algorithm that distributes polls across two Redis instances running on ports 7000 and 7001, routing requests based on the `poll_id`.

Tooling notes

• Uses `HashMap<String, Set<String>>` for the adjacency list to represent the social graph, enabling efficient friendship management.
• Implements a `blockedMap` (`HashMap<String, Set<String>>`) to manage bidirectional user blocking for recommendations.

Architecture in 20 seconds
Three nodes. Each key belongs to one shard by hash(key) modulo 3. Any node can take a request; if it is not the primary for that key it forwards over TCP. The primary writes locally, then sends the write to its replica with a REPLICATE prefix and waits for OK before answering the client. Inside each node it is the same OrderedDict cache with per-key TTL and bounded LRU eviction. One coroutine per client with asyncio, so no locks are needed inside a node.
